stem: The student wants to introduce the glycemic index to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The glycemic index is a scale used in nutrition science.
• It ranks carbohydrate foods by how quickly they raise blood sugar after eating.
• It was developed in 1981 by a team at the University of Toronto led by David Jenkins.
• Pure glucose is assigned a value of 100.
• A related measure, glycemic load, also takes the portion size of a food into account.
choices: The glycemic index was developed in 1981 by a team at the University of Toronto led by David Jenkins.
The glycemic index is a nutrition-science scale that ranks carbohydrate foods by how quickly they raise blood sugar.
Glycemic load, a measure related to the glycemic index, also takes the portion size of a food into account.
The glycemic index is a nutrition-science scale that ranks carbohydrate foods by how much protein they contain.
explanation: A reader who has never heard of the glycemic index first needs to know what it is and what it does. Choice B gives both in one sentence: it labels the index as a nutrition-science scale and says what the scale ranks. This is the core move behind every Rhetorical Synthesis question that asks you to introduce something to an unfamiliar audience. Find the choice that names the thing, attaches a label, and states its purpose.

A.why: You picked a true detail about where the index came from. A reader who doesn't know what the glycemic index is still won't know after reading this sentence. A date and a founder are secondary facts, not an introduction.

C.why: You went to the related measure, which is the subtype's classic trap. This sentence is mostly about glycemic load and treats the glycemic index as something the reader already knows.

D.why: This choice has the right shape, a name plus a label plus a purpose, but the purpose is wrong. The notes say the index ranks foods by how quickly they raise blood sugar, not by their protein content. Check the details of a choice that looks right before you pick it.

stem: The student wants to introduce the Beaufort scale to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Beaufort scale is a system for estimating wind speed.
• It rates wind from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane force).
• Ratings are based on effects an observer can see, such as waves or swaying trees, rather than on instruments.
• It was devised in 1805 by Francis Beaufort, an officer in Britain's Royal Navy.
• Some regions later added levels numbered 13 to 17.
choices: In 1805, Francis Beaufort, an officer in Britain's Royal Navy, devised the scale that now bears his name.
Some regions later added levels numbered 13 to 17 to the Beaufort scale's original top rating of 12.
The Beaufort scale is a system that measures wind speed exactly, using instruments placed on ships and towers.
The Beaufort scale is a system that estimates wind speed by rating visible effects, such as waves, from 0 to 12.
explanation: Your reader doesn't know what the Beaufort scale is, so the sentence has to say so. Choice D labels it as a system for estimating wind speed and briefly explains how it works. Naming the thing and giving its identifying description in one sentence is exactly what the 'introduce to an unfamiliar audience' version of Rhetorical Synthesis rewards.

A.why: You chose the origin story. The sentence tells the reader who made the scale and when, but it never says what the scale measures, so a newcomer still wouldn't know what it is.

B.why: You picked a later development, which is the subtype's trap. Talking about levels added to the scale only makes sense to someone who already knows what the scale is and what its ratings mean.

C.why: This choice labels the scale but gets its method backward. The notes say ratings come from effects an observer can see, not from instruments, and the scale estimates speed rather than measuring it exactly.

stem: The student wants to introduce mezzotint to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Mezzotint is a printmaking technique.
• The artist roughens a metal plate with a toothed tool called a rocker, then smooths some areas to create lighter tones.
• The finished prints show soft shifts from deep black to white.
• The earliest known mezzotint, made by Ludwig von Siegen, dates to 1642.
• In the 1700s, mezzotint was widely used in England to reproduce oil paintings.
choices: Mezzotint is a printmaking technique in which an artist roughens a metal plate, then smooths areas to lighten them.
The earliest known mezzotint, a print made by Ludwig von Siegen, dates to the year 1642.
In the 1700s, mezzotint was widely used in England as a way to reproduce oil paintings.
Mezzotint, the most difficult of all printmaking techniques, was first used by Ludwig von Siegen.
explanation: Someone who has never heard the word 'mezzotint' first needs to know what kind of thing it is. Choice A gives the category label (a printmaking technique) and then says how it works. That label-plus-description pattern is what you look for in Rhetorical Synthesis questions that ask you to introduce something to an unfamiliar audience.

B.why: You picked a date and a name, which is the subtype's trap. The sentence assumes the reader already knows what a mezzotint is and never tells them.

C.why: You chose a later use of the technique. Knowing that mezzotint was popular in 1700s England doesn't tell a newcomer what mezzotint is or how it is made.

D.why: The notes never say mezzotint is the most difficult printmaking technique. You were drawn to a confident-sounding claim the notes don't support. Every word of a correct choice has to come from the notes.

stem: The student wants to introduce the Harris matrix to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A Harris matrix is a type of diagram used in archaeology.
• It shows the order in which the layers at a dig site were deposited, from oldest to most recent.
• It was devised in 1973 by archaeologist Edward C. Harris during excavations in Winchester, England.
• Today, computer programs can draw Harris matrices automatically from excavation records.
choices: Archaeologist Edward C. Harris devised the Harris matrix in 1973 during excavations in Winchester, England.
Today, computer programs can draw Harris matrices automatically from the records kept at a dig site.
A Harris matrix is an archaeological diagram showing the order in which a dig site's layers were deposited.
A Harris matrix is an archaeological map showing exactly where each artifact at a dig site was found.
explanation: A reader new to archaeology needs to know what a Harris matrix is before anything else. Choice C labels it as an archaeological diagram and says what it shows. Leading with an identifying label and the item's purpose is the skill behind Rhetorical Synthesis questions that ask you to introduce something to an unfamiliar audience.

A.why: You chose who made it, when, and where. The sentence names the Harris matrix but never says what it is, so it only works for a reader who already knows.

B.why: You picked a modern development, which is the subtype's trap. Saying that software draws these diagrams treats the Harris matrix as familiar instead of explaining it.

D.why: This choice has the right form but the wrong content. The notes say the diagram shows the order of a site's layers, not where artifacts were found. Make sure the description matches the notes as well as the shape of the answer.
